items.title: What Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO)'s Softer Near-Term Earnings vs Costly Pipeline Means For Shareholders
items.summary: In the past week, Take-Two Interactive Software has faced renewed scrutiny as analysts flagged an expected drop in upcoming quarterly earnings per share and revenue versus last year, against the backdrop of a strong but costly development pipeline. items.title: Does Take Two Interactive Software (TTWO) Justify A Premium On Cash Flow?
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive Software has seen its share price slide in recent months even as its long term return over several years remains positive, which puts a spotlight on whether the cash it can generate truly supports where the stock trades today. With new game releases and franchise updates in the headlines, the real question is how those projects translate into actual cash flows that can justify the current market value. items.title: Why Did Roblox Stock Surge Past The Target An Analyst Just Raised?
items.summary: Roblox (RBLX) stock rose 12.7% in Monday's session. Two things drew the coverage: a developer conference the Friday before, and a price target raise that came with a neutral rating. The problem management named in July was bookings per hour of play.

items.title: Is Take-Two Interactive Stock Underperforming the S&P 500?
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive has trailed the broader S&P 500 over the past year, but Wall Street remains firmly bullish on the stock’s longer-term prospects.

items.title: Roblox Jumps 10% as Wedbush Lifts Target to $48 While Staying Neutral; Take-Two and GameStop Nudge Higher
items.summary: Wedbush raised its price target on Roblox but kept a neutral rating, and the stock immediately shot above that new target. Find out what the analyst said, what Roblox unveiled at its developer conference, and why the risk-reward equation still has Wall Street sitting on the sidelines.

items.title: How Far Could Take-Two Stock Fall In A Market Shock, With Grand Theft Auto VI Still To Come?
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) stock is down 13.4% over the past month, though still up 3.1% over three months. Over the past twelve months it has lost 12.5% while the S&P 500 returned 17.9%. The weakness is not the market's, and the doubt concerns one game, Grand Theft Auto VI, due on November 19.

items.title: GameStop Climbs 4% as Ryan Cohen Buys One Million Shares, Take-Two and Roblox Hold Steady
items.summary: Ryan Cohen just spent his own money buying GameStop shares in the open market, a move that sent the stock surging while its gaming peers barely flinched. Whether that insider signal changes the math on a retailer still losing ground in its core business is a harder question.
